"Tuition fees are paid on behalf of the scholarship holders by the Government of the Czech Republic"
"Scholarship holders have the option of accommodation in student dormitories and meals in student canteens" under the same conditions as Czech citizens
Health care provided by the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic to the same extent as for Czech insured persons
Czech-language route includes a one-year language and preparatory course at the Institute for Language and Preparatory Studies of Charles University (UJOP)
Scholarship amount may be adjusted by MŠMT decision; the valid amount is always stated in the Decision on Granting the Scholarship

Neither a citizen of the Czech Republic nor a citizen of the European Union, and no permanent residence permit in the Czech Republic
Follow-up master's study requires completion of a bachelor's study programme; doctoral study requires completion of a master's study programme
Full-time study only, for the standard length of the accredited programme at a Czech public university

Main call open to applicants not enrolled at a university in the Czech Republic (separate calls exist for students already studying there)
requirements: Electronic application form submitted by 30 September 2026 at the latest via the application register (studyin.gov.cz), with motivation letter; one application per applicant

Attendance at an interview at the responsible Czech embassy (most successful candidates)
Complete documentation uploaded by the deadline set by the embassy so files reach the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT by 15 January 2027
Advanced knowledge of English, proven by the online entrance English language test, for study in English-medium programmes
Czech language command at CEFR B2 level exempts applicants from the one-year preparatory course but still requires passing university admission
documents: Motivation letter - one A4 page for follow-up master's, two A4 pages for doctoral study
CV with a focus on studies and employment
Signed declarations (Guidelines Annexes 1-3): acceptance of scholarship terms, acceptance of health-services terms, affirmation on return to the country of origin
Legalised copy of the birth certificate with certified Czech translation
Medical confirmation of health no more than two months old with certified translation into English or Czech

Legalised copy of the diploma (bachelor's for master's route, master's for doctoral route) with diploma supplement or transcript of completed subjects, with higher-level authentication (apostille/superlegalisation) and certified Czech translation
Overview of study and research stays abroad for the last five years (year, duration, place, purpose)
Doctoral applicants only: overview of publication activity, ideas on the focus of the dissertation thesis (3-5 pages), two letters of recommendation from professors

Final proposals for award are forwarded in January 2027; the decision is delivered to successful applicants through the respective embassy by the end of June 2027
There is no legal claim to the scholarship; scholarships are not transferable to other persons or other academic years
Once granted, neither the university nor the study programme and/or language of study may be changed
coverage: Monthly scholarship CZK 16,000 (follow-up master's) / CZK 24,960 (doctoral), paid usually by the host university in monthly instalments after arrival and admission
Tuition fees paid by the Government of the Czech Republic on behalf of the scholarship holder
Accommodation, food and public transport covered by the holder from the scholarship under the same conditions as Czech citizens
Standard health services reimbursed by the Ministry of Health; the holder pays regulatory fees and co-payments like a Czech insured person
Travel to the Czech Republic and back after graduation is paid by the foreign national or the nominating party - "The MEYS does not reimburse travel expenses"
Applicants should count on initial costs from their own funds of approximately CZK 5,000-8,000 (administrative fees, public transport, settling in)
application_method: Prepare passport, study documents, five-year stay-abroad overview, motivation letter and CV; set up a personal email account

Respond to the embassy invitation to the interview and upload the complete, legalised documentation by the embassy deadline

official.application_route: Single online application through the register at studyin.gov.cz under the Foreign Development Cooperation call, then embassy interview and documentation, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of the 13 listed developing partner countries only; Czech citizens, EU citizens and any foreign national with permanent residence in the Czech Republic may not apply
official.international_eligibility: Yes - intended solely for foreign (non-Czech, non-EU) nationals of the listed countries; international students without permanent residence in the Czech Republic
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Czech-language route: follow-up master's study in selected areas of study recommended per country. English-language route: selected follow-up master's (two-year) and doctoral (three- to four-year) programmes at public universities; files are processed through the responsible Czech embassy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT
official.research_requirement: Doctoral applicants must outline the professional issues of the intended dissertation focus (3-5 pages), provide an overview of publication activity and two letters of recommendation by professors
official.duration: Standard period of full-time study: two-year follow-up master's programmes (Guidelines describe follow-up master's study as two- to three-year-long) in Czech preceded by a one-year preparatory course, or three- to four-year doctoral programmes in English; the exact period is stated in the Decision
official.description: Within its Foreign Development Cooperation programme, the Government of the Czech Republic funds nationals of designated partner states to complete the standard period of full-time study at Czech public universities - a follow-up master's or doctoral programme in English, or a master's in Czech preceded by a one-year language and preparatory course. The programme is run by the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Health, and administered by the Czech National Agency for International Education and Research (DZS).
official.program_type: Government development-cooperation scholarship under Government Resolution No. 870 (2025-2030 development scholarship strategy)
official.english_requirement: Advanced knowledge of English, proven by passing the compulsory online entrance English language test submitted with the application (no IELTS/TOEFL score published); the General Academic Prerequisites Test is also compulsory for English-medium applicants

Any allowance beyond the published monthly rate (e.g. during the preparatory year or thesis completion) - not stated on the official pages
verification.notes: Amounts, tuition statement, travel rule and deadlines cross-checked between the MŠMT call page, the binding Guidelines (Issue No. 1, August 2026, effective 21 August 2026), the studyin.gov.cz call listing for 2027/2028 and the DZS programme page. fully_funded set false because the official pages state travel expenses are not reimbursed and accommodation and food are paid out of the monthly stipend.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a state development scholarship, not a university contract: you file once through the national register at studyin.gov.cz, finish two online tests by 30 September, and only shortlisted candidates face an embassy interview and must assemble a heavily legalised document set by mid-January. The money is a monthly CZK stipend (CZK 16,000 master's, CZK 24,960 doctoral) paid by the host university after you enrol, while the Government settles tuition directly - so you must fund flights, roughly CZK 5,000-8,000 of first-month settlement costs, and accommodation and food out of the stipend. The whole chance is one 5-6 week September window per year, with decisions only the following June, so plan a gap year rather than an immediate start.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bachelor's or master's graduates from the 13 listed partner countries who can commit to a full-time 2027/2028 start at a Czech public university and accept a modest, living-cost stipend with no travel money.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your passport's country is on the current 13-country list and that you hold no Czech permanent residence before investing in document legalisation
Start the apostille/superlegalisation and sworn Czech translation of your diploma, transcript and birth certificate months early - these outlive the application window
Get a medical certificate issued less than two months before the embassy documentation deadline, already translated
Draft the motivation letter around practical application of the learning and the benefit to your home country, not academic interest alone
Book both online tests early in the September window - an application without both mandatory tests is not processed at all
Compile the five-year list of study and research stays abroad (year, length, place, purpose) before opening the form
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the form but never completing both compulsory tests - the system does not forward the application for evaluation
Citizenship of a country not on the current annual list, or holding permanent residence in the Czech Republic, which voids eligibility outright
Complete documentation arriving late: files must reach the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and MŠMT by 15 January 2027, with each embassy setting its own earlier cut-off
Applying for a level already completed - master's graduates cannot be funded for another or lower master's
Missing apostille/superlegalisation or certified Czech translations, which universities and the embassy treat as non-existent documents
Assuming you can switch programme, university or language of study after the award - none of these can be changed
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to and from the Czech Republic (explicitly not reimbursed), roughly CZK 5,000-8,000 of initial administrative and settling-in costs, accommodation, food and public transport paid out of the monthly stipend, health-care co-payments and regulatory fees, and any fees for extending study beyond the standard period.
document_audit: Diploma, diploma supplement/transcript and birth certificate need legalisation plus a certified Czech translation - a sworn-English translation is only a fallback where Czech translation is impossible
The medical certificate has a two-month freshness window measured against the documentation stage, not the application date
Apostille covers Hague Convention states; other documents face full superlegalisation through the foreign ministry and the Czech embassy
For doctoral routes add a publication list, a 3-5 page dissertation focus outline and two professor recommendation letters - missing any of these stalls the file at the embassy
Applicants already resident in the Czech Republic bypass the embassy route and file directly with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs by 15 January
alerts: Eligibility is tied to an annually refreshed country list - the 13 countries for 2027/2028 will not necessarily repeat in the next call
The call carries an age window (born after 01.09.1991 and before 31.08.2008) that applicants routinely overlook
Only one registration and one application per applicant; duplicate entries invalidate the file
Payment stops if you are absent from the Czech Republic for more than 30 consecutive days (half-pay beyond 15 days), and terminates if you obtain permanent residence or interrupt study
The 30 September 2026 window is already closed - the next realistic application point is the call expected around August-September 2027
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register at studyin.gov.cz under the Foreign Development Cooperation call, complete the e-form and motivation letter, finish the online tests by 30 September, attend the embassy interview and upload the legalised document set by the embassy deadline (15 January 2027 at the latest), and await the decision delivered through the embassy by the end of June 2027.
